# Base Types

<!-- purpose: Where Base Types files live, the kinds they hold and every key they accept -->

*This page is generated from SWCraft's own definitions, and describes the version you have installed.*

Base types, one file each under `data_types/base/`: how the platform stores a value — its size, its encoding and its C declaration. One kind, `base_type`, which a `value_type` names as its `base` and which no data element, argument, record field or array element names. The directory is mandatory and may be empty.

One file per `base_type`, in `data_types/base/` under the model root, named after its `name` and ending in `.yaml`. Where that file name is already taken by another element's file — compared without regard to case — the file gets the nearest free `~1`, `~2`, … instead; the element is identified by the `name` inside the file, never by its file name.

## `base_type` { #base_type }

<!-- purpose: Writing `base_type` files in Base Types: each key, its type and default -->

A base type: how the platform stores a value — its size in bits, its encoding and its C declaration — emitted as a `SW-BASE-TYPE`. A base type is never what a data prototype is typed by (AUTOSAR's `AutosarDataPrototype.type`): no data element, argument, record field or array element may name one. A base type is an element of its own layer, `base_types`, so it may share its name with a type of another layer. A `value_type` names it as its `base`, and the data prototypes name the `value_type`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The type's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/base/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the base types, must not be blank, and immutable. |
| `kind` | string, one of `base_type` | yes | — | Always `base_type`. The layer holds one kind and is not discriminated; the field is an ordinary literal, kept, immutable as it was, so a base type file reads as it did when base types were a kind of the data types layer. |
| `size` | integer (bits) | yes | — | The size of the base type, in bits. Must be > 0. |
| `encoding` | string | yes | — | A required AUTOSAR BASE-TYPE-ENCODING token (NONE, 2C, IEEE754, ...); must not be blank, because a blank one is not round-trippable through the ARXML importer. |
| `native_declaration` | string | no | `""` | The C type name the generated code declares for this base type (for example `uint8_t`), emitted exactly as written as its `NATIVE-DECLARATION`. Required by check-model: SWCraft never derives one, so a base type without it still loads, but check-model reports it and ARXML generation refuses it until it is filled in. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the type. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |
| `package` | string | no | absent | The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/Base`, its layer's package, this base type is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the base type and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/Base/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/Base` itself. SWCraft's importers record it for an element whose source path is exactly `/DataTypes/Base/{package}/{name}`, SWCraft's own layout, so a project's export imports back placed; and for an element that would otherwise share `/DataTypes/Base` with a name differing from its own only in case. An author may set it to place an element or to resolve such a collision. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule. |
